ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.claim: The fate of a wealthy Jewish capitalist shows that God grants favors, though the wretched attribute them to their own ability and idols.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r6.anchor: The fate of a capitalist Jew is mentioned.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p328/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p328/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p328/r5.claim: A long account says Qārūn paid a woman to accuse Moses, she repented and exposed him, and the earth swallowed Qārūn and his followers; the author says God knows that story best.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p328/r5.anchor: فأمر الله الأرض أن تطيعه، فقال: يا أرض خذيه وأتباعه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r1.claim: One explanation connects the sinking directly to Qarun's arrogance, insolence, and excess; the verse's فاء signals this causal relation.
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r1.anchor: لما أشر وبطر وعتا خسف الله به وبداره الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r2.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r2.claim: Report says Qarun, angered by Moses's levy, bribed a woman to accuse him; she confessed, and Moses ordered earth to swallow Qarun and companions despite pleas. God rebuked him; Israelites suspected greed, and Qarun sinks a hundred qāma daily.
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r2.anchor: قيل إن قارون كان يؤذي نبي الله موسى عليه السلام كل وقت وهو يداريه للقرابة التي بينهما حتى نزلت الزكاة

RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r3.claim: Al-Qadi says Qarun's descent to the seventh earth or any lesser depth is not impossible if the report is understood as rhetorical exaggeration meant to deter.
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r3.anchor: إذا هلك بالخسف فسواء نزل عن ظاهر الأرض إلى الأرض السابعة

RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r4.claim: Razi finds it unlikely that God would have answered their pleas if they had called on Him, unless the plea included repentance: they persisted in wrongdoing, and Moses acted under God's command.
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r4.anchor: فإن صح حمل على استغاثة مقرونة بالتوبة

RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r5.claim: Razi rejects the claims that Qarun sinks endlessly and by a specified number of measures each day, since descent must have an end and the stated number is equally doubtful.
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r5.anchor: وقولهم إنه يتجلجل في الأرض أبدا فبعيد لأنه لا بد له من نهاية

RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r6.claim: Razi considers these isolated, conflicting reports of little use and unable to establish certainty; since this is not a practical ruling, he prefers relying on the Qur'an and leaving further details to God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p16#2/r6.anchor: والذي عندي في أمثال هذه الحكايات أنها قليلة الفائدة لأنها من باب أخبار الآحاد فلا تفيد اليقين

RAZI-FULL:v25p17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p17/r1.claim: The phrase means Qarun could neither avenge himself on Moses nor fend off God's punishment; انتصر is to protect oneself from an adversary's aid or force.
RAZI-FULL:v25p17/r1.anchor: من المنتقمين من موسى أو من الممتنعين من عذاب

BURSEVI:v6p315#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p315#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p315#3/r1.claim: Khasafa for a place means to sink into the earth; for the moon, its light disappears; a sunken eye loses sharpness, and the preposition ba makes the verb transitive.
BURSEVI:v6p315#3/r1.anchor: يقال : خسف المكان يخسف خسوفا ذهب في الأرض كما في "القاموس" وخسف القمر زال ضوءه

BURSEVI:v6p315#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p315#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v6p315#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun balked at the zakat agreed for his fortune, arranged a woman's false charge against Moses, but she confessed; after God authorized Moses to command earth, it swallowed Qarun and his followers despite their pleas.
BURSEVI:v6p315#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : لما نزلت الزكاة على موسى صالحه على أن يعطيه

BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r1.claim: A fiʾa is a mutually supportive group; the word comes from fāʾa, to return, since its members return to one another for mutual aid.
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r1.anchor: قال الراغب : الفئة الجماعة المتظاهرة التي يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض في التعاضد انتهى من فاء ، أي رجع

BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r2.claim: They would support Qarun by trying to ward off the punishment of being swallowed by the earth.

BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r3.claim: The phrase describes helpers who are beyond or apart from God's aid.
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r3.anchor: {من دون الله} أي : حال كونهم متجاوزين نصرة الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r4.claim: Qarun could not resist or escape the punishment in any way; naṣara someone against an enemy means to protect him, and intasara means to protect oneself.
BURSEVI:v6p316#2/r4.anchor: {وما كان من المنتصرين} أي من الممتنعين عنه بوجه من الوجوه يقال نصره من عدوه فانتصر

STUDYQURAN:28:81/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:81/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:81/r1.claim: Commentators relate that Korah’s enmity, rebellion, and slander against Moses led God to grant Moses power to call for the earth to swallow Korah.
STUDYQURAN:28:81/r1.anchor: God granted the latter the power to call upon the earth to swallow him (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:28:81/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:81/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:81/r2.claim: Fiʾah, rendered “party,” can denote a group one can call upon for support in battle.
STUDYQURAN:28:81/r2.anchor: refers to a group upon whom one can call for support in a battle (see 8:15–16c)

TAB-FULL:v18p331#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p331#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p331#3/r1.claim: Qarun’s companions were with him in his house and shared his hypocrisy and support for harming Moses.
TAB-FULL:v18p331#3/r1.anchor: في داره، وكانوا جماعة جلوسا معه، وهم على مثل الذي هو عليه من النفاق والمؤازرة على أذى موسى

TAB-FULL:v18p331#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p331#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p331#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that Qarun, fearing Moses’ zakat demand, arranged a false accusation with a paid woman; God swallowed Qarun and his followers in stages after she exposed him. The report cites 28:79, 23:117 and 28:83.
TAB-FULL:v18p331#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما نزلت الزكاة أتى قارون موسى، فصالحه على كل ألف دينار دينارا، وكل ألف شيء شيئا

TAB-FULL:v18p334/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p334/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p334/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after Qarun’s paid woman falsely accused Moses of sex, she confessed his innocence; Moses commanded the earth to swallow them, and God later rebuked Moses for not answering the Israelites when they sought relief.
TAB-FULL:v18p334/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: " لما أمر الله موسى بالزكاة، قال: رموه بالزنا

TAB-FULL:v18p335/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p335/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث
TAB-FULL:v18p335/r1.claim: Abd Allah ibn al-Harith recounts Qarun’s hostility toward Moses, the plot to frame him with a woman, her repentance and exposure of the plot, and the staged sinking of Qarun, his house and companions. The report also cites Solomon’s story (27:38 and 27:40).
TAB-FULL:v18p335/r1.anchor: قال: خرج عبد الله بن الحارث من الدار، ودخل المقصورة؛ فلما خرج منها، جلس وتساند عليها

TAB-FULL:v18p338/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r1.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r1.claim: Abu Imran al-Jawni says it reached him that God told Moses the earth would never again obey anyone after him.
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r1.anchor: عن أبي عمران الجوني، قال: بلغني أنه قيل لموسى: لا أعبد الأرض لأحد بعدك أبدا

TAB-FULL:v18p338/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the earth into which Qarun sank as the seventh earth.
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، ولم يذكر ابن مهدي أبا نصر: " {فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض} [القصص: 81] قال: الأرض السابعة

TAB-FULL:v18p338/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that Qarun sinks one hundred fathoms each day and continues to descend until the Resurrection without reaching the earth’s bottom.
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: بلغنا أنه يخسف به كل يوم مائة قامة، ولا يبلغ أسفل الأرض إلى يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v18p338/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r4.speaker: مالك بن دينار
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r4.claim: Malik ibn Dinar reports hearing that Qarun sinks one hundred fathoms each day.
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r4.anchor: عن جعفر بن سليمان، قال: سمعت مالك بن دينار، قال: بلغني أن قارون يخسف به كل يوم مائة قامة

TAB-FULL:v18p338/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r5.claim: Qatadah reports that Qarun sinks one fathom each day, continuing to descend without reaching the bottom until the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v18p338/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، " {فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض} [القصص: 81] ذكر لنا أنه يخسف به كل يوم قامة

TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r1.claim: Qatadah glosses the absent faction as an army and says Qarun had no protection with which to shield himself from God.
TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: " {فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه} [القصص: 81] أي جند ينصرونه، وما عنده منعة يمتنع بها من الله

TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r2.claim: فئة is a group a person resorts to for help against an enemy, then any group that supports him; its root evokes returning to someone in need.
TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r2.anchor: وأصلها الجماعة التي يفيء إليها الرجل عند الحاجة إليهم، للعون على العدو، ثم تستعمل ذلك العرب في كل جماعة كانت عونا للرجل

TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p338#2/r3.claim: Khuffaf’s verse uses فئة for a strong, supportive group able to stand firm against hardships.

TABATABAI:28:81-83/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r1.claim: Both pronouns refer to Qarun, and the sinking follows from his wrongdoing.
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r1.anchor: الضميران لقارون والجملة متفرعة على بغيه

TABATABAI:28:81-83/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r2.claim: A فئة is a group whose members gravitate toward one another; victory and resistance carry the sense of protection and holding off harm.
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r2.anchor: الفئة الجماعة يميل بعضهم إلى بعض

TABATABAI:28:81-83/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r3.claim: No group could shield Qarun from punishment and he could not resist it; his wealth and strength, supposedly gained by knowledge, failed without God and showed God had granted his riches.
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r3.anchor: فما كان له جماعة يمنعونه العذاب وما كان من الممتنعين على خلاف ما كان يظن

TABATABAI:28:81-83/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:81-83/r4.claim: The فاء makes the lack of rescuers a consequence of the sinking: the event exposes Qarun's false claims of deserving wealth and independence from God.

TABATABAI:28:76-84/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that Qarun arranged a false accusation of adultery against Moses; after the woman confessed the plot, Moses commanded the earth to swallow Qarun and his people despite their pleas, and God said He would have answered them had they called Him. Ibn Abbas identifies this as the sinking in the verse.
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وذلك قوله تعالى { فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض }

TABATABAI:28:76-84/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r2.speaker: ابن نوفل الهاشمي
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r2.claim: A version transmitted by Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim says the woman was brought before Qarun and Israel to accuse Moses, but confessed the truth; Moses complained to God, who empowered him over Qarun.
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r2.anchor: عن عبد الرزاق وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن نوفل الهاشمي القصة لكن فيها أن المرأة

TABATABAI:28:76-84/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r3.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r3.claim: Al-Qummi's version says Moses brought Qarun the zakat ruling, Qarun mocked and expelled him, and Moses complained to God, who caused Qarun and his house to sink.
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r3.anchor: وروى القمي في تفسيره في القصة أن موسى عليه السلام جاء إلى قارون وبلغه حكم الزكاة

TABATABAI:28:76-84/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r4.claim: Al-Tabataba'i calls the al-Qummi report mawquf and containing objectionable matters, which is why he leaves it unquoted; the Ibn Abbas and Ibn Nawfal reports are also mawquf.
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r4.anchor: والرواية موقوفة مشتملة على أمور منكرة ولذلك تركنا نقلها كما إن روايتي ابن عباس وابن نوفل أيضا موقوفتان

TABATABAI:28:76-84/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r5.claim: The Ibn Abbas story centers on Qarun's wrongdoing against Moses, whereas the Qur'anic account says he wronged the Israelites; the verse also points to learned, acquired know-how, apparently the means of making wealth.
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r5.anchor: على أن رواية ابن عباس تقصص بغيه على موسى عليه السلام والذي تقصه الآيات بغيه على بنى إسرائيل

TABATABAI:28:76-84/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r6.claim: The present Torah recounts the rebellion differently, naming Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and On with 250 leaders who oppose Moses; the cited account is Numbers chapter 16.
TABATABAI:28:76-84/r6.anchor: ففي الإصحاح السادس عشر من سفر العدد وأخذ قورح بن بصهار بن نهات بن لاوي وداثان وأبيرام

TABRISI:28:76-82/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82/r1.speaker: حفص عن عاصم ويعقوب وسهل
TABRISI:28:76-82/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, Yaʿqūb, and Sahl read with fatḥ on khāʾ and sīn.
TABRISI:28:76-82/r1.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم ويعقوب وسهل لخسف الخاء والسين

TABRISI:28:76-82/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82/r2.speaker: الحسن والأعرج وشيبة ومجاهد
TABRISI:28:76-82/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Shayba, and Mujāhid also read with fatḥ on khāʾ and sīn.
TABRISI:28:76-82/r2.anchor: وهو قراءة الحسن والأعرج وشيبة ومجاهد

TABRISI:28:76-82/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82/r3.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:28:76-82/r3.claim: The remaining readers use the passive form, with ḍamma on khāʾ and kasra on sīn.
TABRISI:28:76-82/r3.anchor: والباقون لخسف بضم الخاء وكسر السين

TABRISI:28:76-82/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:76-82/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:28:76-82/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the active reading follows the preceding mention of God; the passive form reaches the same meaning.
TABRISI:28:76-82/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: من قرأ الخسف بنا بفتح الخاء فلتقدم ذكر الله تعالى

TABRISI:28:79-81/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:79-81/r14.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:28:79-81/r14.claim: Al-Suddī says Qarun paid an Israelite prostitute two thousand to falsely accuse Moses of soliciting her before the Israelites; she regretted it and exposed Qarun’s slander plot and marked money.
TABRISI:28:79-81/r14.anchor: قال السدي: دعا قارون امرأة من بني إسرائيل بغيا فقال لها إني أعطيك ألفين

TABRISI:28:81-82/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:81-82/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:81-82/r1.claim: After the woman exposed Qarun’s slander, Moses invoked God, who made the earth obey him. It swallowed Qarun and his bed by stages despite his pleas for kinship; God says Qarun would have been saved had he called on Him.
TABRISI:28:81-82/r1.anchor: فعرف بنو إسرائيل خاتم قارون فغضب موسى فدعا الله عليه

TABRISI:28:81-82/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:81-82/r2.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:28:81-82/r2.claim: Muqātil says the Israelites accused Moses of swallowing Qarun to inherit his wealth because they were cousins; his house and all property were swallowed three days later and never recovered.
TABRISI:28:81-82/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: ولما أمر موسى الأرض فابتلعته

TABRISI:28:81-82/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:81-82/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:81-82/r3.claim: No group devoted to Qarun could ward off God’s punishment; he had trusted his retinue and troops but could not save himself either.
TABRISI:28:81-82/r3.anchor: لأنه كان يقدر مع نفسه الامتناع بحاشيته وجنوده

THALABI:v7p262#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p262#2/r12.speaker: العلماء بأخبار القدماء
THALABI:v7p262#2/r12.claim: Scholars of ancient reports describe Qarun as Israel's most learned man after Moses and Aaron, a fine reciter of Torah, handsome and wealthy, who allied hypocritically with Samiri and transgressed.
THALABI:v7p262#2/r12.anchor: قال العلماء بأخبار القدماء: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون، وأقرأهم للتوراة وأجملهم وأغناهم ولكنه نافق السامري

THALABI:v7p264/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p264/r1.speaker: قارون
THALABI:v7p264/r1.claim: Qarun dismisses the event as no more astonishing than Moses' sorcery.
THALABI:v7p264/r1.anchor: فقال قارون: والله ما هذا بأعجب مما تصنع من السحر

THALABI:v7p264/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p264/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p264/r2.claim: Qarun angrily separated from Moses, who treated him gently because of kinship, while Qarun harassed him and grew arrogant; Qarun built a gold-doored, gold-plated house where Israelite notables ate and socialized.
THALABI:v7p264/r2.anchor: فذهب قارون مغاضبا واعتزل موسى بأتباعه

THALABI:v7p264/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p264/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p264/r3.claim: When Moses imposed zakat, Qarun agreed to pay one per thousand of each kind of wealth, but found the total too high and turned the Israelites against Moses by alleging he wanted their property.
THALABI:v7p264/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ثم إن الله سبحانه وتعالى أنزل الزكاة على موسى

THALABI:v7p264/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p264/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p264/r4.claim: Qarun recruited a prostitute to accuse Moses of adultery; the reported payment varies between a thousand dirhams, a thousand dinars, a gold basin, or her price, and she confessed Qarun had paid her.
THALABI:v7p264/r4.anchor: فقال: آمركم أن تجيئوا بفلانة البغي فنجعل لها جعلا على أن تقذفه بنفسها

THALABI:v7p264/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p264/r5.speaker: موسى
THALABI:v7p264/r5.claim: In Ibn Abbas's narrative, Moses states penalties of hand amputation for theft, eighty lashes for false accusation, one hundred lashes for an unmarried adulterer, and stoning for a married adulterer.
THALABI:v7p264/r5.anchor: من سرق قطعنا يده ومن افترى جلدناه ثمانين

THALABI:v7p264/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p264/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p264/r6.claim: The woman swore by God who split the sea and revealed the Torah, then chose repentance and exposed Qarun's scheme; Moses prayed for justice, God allowed him to command earth, and he separated Qarun's followers from his own.
THALABI:v7p264/r6.anchor: فلما ناشدها تداركها الله بالتوفيق وقالت في نفسها: لئن أحدث اليوم توبة أفضل من أن أوذي رسول الله

THALABI:v7p265/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p265/r1.speaker: موسى
THALABI:v7p265/r1.claim: Moses first commands the earth to swallow Qarun and his companions to their necks, then orders it to take them fully.
THALABI:v7p265/r1.anchor: يا أرض خذيهم، فأخذتهم إلى الأعناق، وقارون وأصحابه في كل ذلك لا يلتفت إليه

THALABI:v7p265/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p265/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
THALABI:v7p265/r2.claim: God rebukes Moses for not showing mercy when the victims called to him seventy times, saying that had they called on God, He would have answered nearby.
THALABI:v7p265/r2.anchor: وأوحى الله تعالى إلى موسى: يا موسى ما أفظك. استغاثوا بك سبعين مرة فلم ترحمهم ولم تغثهم

THALABI:v7p265/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p265/r3.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v7p265/r3.claim: Qatada reports that Qarun sinks one stature every day, moving through the earth without reaching its bottom until Resurrection.
THALABI:v7p265/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: وذكر [لنا] أنه يخسف به كل يوم قامة

THALABI:v7p265/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p265/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p265/r4.claim: The Israelites suspected Moses had cursed Qarun to acquire his house and treasure, so Moses prayed for the house and wealth to sink too.
THALABI:v7p265/r4.anchor: قالوا: وأصبحت بنو إسرائيل يتناجون فيما بينهم أن [موسى] إنما دعا على قارون

THALABI:v7p265/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p265/r5.speaker: الله سبحانه
THALABI:v7p265/r5.claim: God tells Moses that He will never make the earth obey anyone else after him, explaining the swallowing of Qarun and his house.
THALABI:v7p265/r5.anchor: وأوحى الله سبحانه إلى موسى: إني لا أعبد الأرض لأحد بعدك أبدا، فذلك قوله تعالى: فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض

THALABI:v7p265/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p265/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p265/r6.claim: The phrase about Qarun not being among those who can defend themselves describes people able to ward off punishment.
THALABI:v7p265/r6.anchor: فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان من المنتصرين الممتنعين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī refers readers to his discussion of the meaning of خسف in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r1.anchor: ذكرنا معنى الخسف في سورة: سبحان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r2.claim: Muqātil and Qatāda report that Qarun sinks into the earth by a man’s height each day until the Resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل وقتادة: فهو يتجلجل في الأرض كل يوم قامة رجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Qarun was sunk to the lowest earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: خسف به إلى الأرض السفلى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r4.claim: Muqātil says Israelites accused Moses of sinking Qarun to seize his property; three days later God sank Qarun’s house and stored wealth too.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r4.anchor: قال مقاتل: لما خسف الله بقارون، قالت بنو إسرائيل: إن موسى إنما أهلك قارون ليأخذ ماله وداره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r5.claim: He had no band of soldiers to protect him from God and could not defend himself against the sinking.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r5.anchor: يقول: لم يكن له جند يمنعونه من الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r6.claim: Al-Wāḥidī defines المنتصر as one who has attained the state of victory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p465/r6.anchor: والمنتصر: الذي قد بلغ حالة النصرة

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r4.claim: Qarun was swallowed by the earth with his home and wealth; those who had envied him regretted it, accepted God’s provision, and recognized that the ungrateful do not prosper.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r4.anchor: Karun, evi barkı ve bütün servetiyle birlikte yerin dibine batırıldı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r5.claim: Qarun’s story remains a warning to those who trust wealth and power, consider themselves privileged and great, disobey God, wrong others, and transgress.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:78/r5.anchor: Karun kıssası, servet ve gücüne güvenerek, kendini imtiyazlı ve büyük görüp Allah’a isyan, insanlara karşı haksızlık eden

BAQILLANI:v1p193/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r6.claim: The account of Qārūn's sinking is another example of harmonious composition, compressed into three exceptional phrases.
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r6.anchor: ومن المؤتلف قوله ( ﴿ فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان من المنتصرين ﴾ )

BAQILLANI:v1p193/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r8.claim: Quranic story passages compress narratives together with admonitions, proverbs, wisdom, proofs of oneness, and declarations of God's transcendence; expanded prose would be heavier and less coherent.
BAQILLANI:v1p193/r8.anchor: كل سورة من هذه السور تتضمن من القصص ما لو تكلفت العبارة عنها بأضعاف كلماتها لم تستوف ما استوفت

BAQILLANI:v1p276/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r1.claim: The author accepts that the simile passage is inimitable through its wording, order, and composition, but does not attribute its inimitability to the simile itself.
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r1.anchor: فأما الآية التي فيها ذكر التشبيه فان ادعى إعجازها لألفاظها

BAQILLANI:v1p276/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r2.claim: Quranic inimitability attaches to its supreme clarity and eloquence, not to one genre of expression; the Quran repeatedly calls itself a clarification and clear Arabic speech.
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r2.anchor: فكرر في مواضع جل ذكره انه مبين

BAQILLANI:v1p276/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r3.claim: The Quran's effect on listeners depends on its arrangement, placement, and openings and endings; powerful speech can move hearts across a wide range of emotions and prompt courage and generosity.
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r3.anchor: وبحسب ما يترتب في نظمه ويتنزل في موقعه

BAQILLANI:v1p276/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r4.claim: Speech also reveals its speaker: love poetry is more tender from a true lover, while affectation exposes a pretender; battle poetry from a brave person shows its genuine source.
BAQILLANI:v1p276/r4.anchor: ألا ترى أن الشعر في الغزل إذا صدر عن محب كان أرق وأحسن وإذا صدر عن متعمل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p235/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p235/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p235/r1.claim: An attribute gains grandeur when implied rather than stated directly; praise can be conveyed by assigning it to something that encompasses or accompanies the person.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p235/r1.anchor: وكما أن الصفة إذا لم تأتك مصرحا بذكرها ، مكشوفا عن وجهها ، ولكن مدلولا بغيرها ، كان ذلك أفخم لشأنها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p235/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p235/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p235/r2.claim: Ziyad al-Aʿjam's poem implies that Ibn al-Ḥarshaj possesses generosity by placing generosity, nobility, and liberality in the dome erected over him; stating the traits directly would sound flat.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p235/r2.anchor: ومثاله قول زياد الأعجم ، + الكامل + : ( إن السماحة والمروءة والندى في قبة ضربت على ابن الحشرج )

MAJAZ:v2p111/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p111/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p111/r4.claim: Fiʾah means a group of helpers and supporters. Khafaf’s poem uses it for a strong, discerning band.
MAJAZ:v2p111/r4.anchor: «فما كان له من فئة» (81) أي من أعوان وظهراء، قال خفاف :

SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r1.claim: The common reading has kasra on the pronoun because of the preceding kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r1.anchor: قوله: { فخسفنا به وبداره }: المشهور كسر هاء الكناية في " به " و " بداره " لأجل كسر ما قبلها.

SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r2.claim: A variant has the pronoun's original damma and is Hijazi.
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r2.anchor: وقرىء بضمها,. وقد تقدم أنها الأصل، وهي لغة الحجاز.

SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r3.claim: If كان is incomplete, من فئة is its subject and له or ينصرونه its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r3.anchor: يجوز أن تكون اسم كان، إن كانت ناقصة، و " له " الخبر، أو " ينصرونه " ،

SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r4.claim: If كان is complete, من فئة is subject, ينصرونه modifies فئة, and من is extra.
SAMIN-DURR:28:81/r4.anchor: وأن تكون فاعلة إن كانت تامة، و " ينصرونه " صفة ل " فئة " فيحكم على موضعها بالجر لفظا وبالرفع معنى؛ لأن " من " مزيدة فيها.

ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r9.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p153/r9.claim: Moses ordered earth to swallow Qarun and his house in stages, from knees to navel to neck, until both sank.

ASAD-NOTES:28:81#n91/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:81#n91/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:81#n91/r1.claim: The phrase literally says Qarun had no host at all to aid him.
ASAD-NOTES:28:81#n91/r1.anchor: Lit., "he had no host whatever to succour him ... , etc.

ASAD-NOTES:28:81#n91/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:81#n91/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:81#n91/r2.claim: Asad allows that the earth swallowing Qarun may metaphorically describe a sudden catastrophic loss of all his wealth and former grandeur.
ASAD-NOTES:28:81#n91/r2.anchor: may possibly be a metaphor of a catastrophic, unforeseen loss - from whatever cause - of all his worldly goods

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p116/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p116/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p116/r1.claim: Bint quotes an example of al-muʾtalif in which the three words of Qarun's destruction are each praised as rarer than red sulfur.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p116/r1.anchor: وهذه ثلاث كلمات، كل كلمة منها أعز من الكبريت الأحمر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r1.claim: Bint presents al-Bāqillānī's conclusion that the Qurʾān is the highest form of expression, combining balanced and sound order, beauty, ease on the tongue, pleasing sound, psychological acceptance, vividness, and demonstrative force.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r1.anchor: إلى أين وصل الباقلاني في بيان إعجاز القرآن من جهة البلاغة، بعد طول الجهد وعناء النقل للمطولات من القصائد والخطب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r2.claim: Al-Bāqillānī says elevated speech can unsettle or console, delight or grieve, move listeners, and prompt courage and generosity because it has subtle paths into hearts.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r2.anchor: وإذا علا الكلام في نفسه كان له من الوقع في القلوب والتمكن في النفوس، ما يذهل ويبهج، ويقلق ويؤنس

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r3.claim: Al-Bāqillānī says speech's effects depend on its arrangement, placement, opening and ending; its sources shape its effects, and its language signals the speaker's standing and stature.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p118/r3.anchor: وبحسب ما يترتب في نظمه ويتنزل في موقعه، ويجرى على سمت مطلعه ومقطعه، يكون عجيب تأثيراته وبديع مقتضياته

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r1.claim: Qārūn’s exemplary fate admonishes people seduced by worldly riches who forget God and the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p568/r1.anchor: people who were lured by the riches of this world and had forgotte n God and the Hereafter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p574/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p574/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p574/r1.claim: The account suppresses that, after the Samiri episode, Moses challenged Qārūn and his companions to a mutual imprecation by the worship tent; Numbers 16:27–34 describes the earth swallowing the challengers and their households.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p574/r1.anchor: invited Q ārūn and his companions to a mub āhalah (cursing and ill-praying) in front of the worship tent

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p574/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p574/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p574/r2.claim: Qārūn and his companions were swallowed by the earth following Moses' prayer, leaving Qārūn unable to defend himself and his people unable to rescue him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p574/r2.anchor: Q ārūn and his companions were submerged in the earth as a result of the curse and prayer of Moses

NASHR:v1p416/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p416/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p416/r1.claim: Before alif-lām, a transferred vowel does not restore a preceding madd letter or the original sukun; the consonant is moved and the madd is omitted, a rule agreed by reciters despite Arabic alternatives.
NASHR:v1p416/r1.anchor: أنه إذا كان قبل لام التعريف المنقول إليها حرف من حروف المد، أو ساكن غيرهن لم يجز إثبات حرف المد

QIRAAT-ER:28:81:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:81:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:81:13#1/r1.claim: A ten-reader variant removes hamza and replaces it with yāʾ, reflecting dialectal hamza avoidance without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:28:81:13#1/r1.anchor: Hamza removal: fiʾatin→fiyatin; canonical 10-reader variant; hamza replaced by yāʾ

ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Qarun, Moses' cousin and a learned man, rebelled and refused the zakat; he stirred the Israelites against Moses, arranged a woman's false accusation, and she confessed the bribe and affirmed Moses' prophethood. Hakim graded the report sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r1.anchor: وابن أبي حاتم والحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن قارون كان ابن عم موسى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r2.claim: Alusi records variants that Qarun paid the woman either a thousand dinars or a gold basin filled with gold to accuse Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r2.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أنه جعل للبغي ألف دينار وقيل : طستا من ذهب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r3.claim: Other versions say Moses asked God for power over the earth, which swallowed Qarun and his followers progressively as they begged; God reproached Moses for refusing their pleas, and one version has Moses say he acted in anger for God.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p122#2/r3.anchor: يا موسى سألك عبادك وتضرعوا اليك فلم تجبهم وعزتي لو أنهم دعوني لأجبتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r1.claim: When Israelites alleged that Moses sank Qarun to inherit from him, Moses prayed to God, who sank Qarun's house and wealth as well.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r1.anchor: إنما فعل موسى عليه السلام به ذلك ليرثه فدعا الله تعالى حتى خسف بداره وأمواله

ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r2.claim: Some reports say Qarun and his house sank at the same time, and his house was made of gold plates.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r2.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار أن الخسف به وبداره كان في زمان واحد وكانت داره فيما قيل : من صفائح الذهب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r3.claim: Several reports say Qarun sinks a stature each day and keeps descending until the Resurrection; Alusi finds this difficult if the philosophers' estimate of Earth's diameter and lack of motion are correct.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r3.anchor: وجاء في عدة آثار أنه يخسف به كل يوم قامة وأن يتجلجل في الأرض لا يبلغ قعرها إلى يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r4.claim: Alusi says sinking is possible both inherently and in occurrence, with its ordinary cause explained elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r4.anchor: وأما الخسف فلا شك في امكانه الذاتي والوقوعي وسببه العادي مبين في محله

ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r5.claim: One derivation connects فئة with فأوت قلبه, a root with an omitted final radical: a group is so called because its members incline toward one another; من is extra in the construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r5.anchor: فئة أي جماعة معينة مشتقة من فأوت قلبه إذا ميلته وسميت الجماعة بذلك لميل بعضهم إلى بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r6.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r6.claim: Al-Raghib instead derives فئة from الفيء, return, and says it has an omitted middle radical because members of a group return to one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r6.anchor: وقال الراغب : إنه محذوف العين فوزنه فلة وأنه من الفيء وهو الرجوع لأن بعض الجماعة يرجع إلى بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r7.claim: The verse means Qarun had no group to rescue him from God's punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r7.anchor: ينصرونه من دون الله ( بدفع العذاب عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r8.claim: He could not defend himself; alternatively, the phrase stresses that he could not gain victory even with his helpers.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p123/r8.anchor: من المنتصرين ( أي الممتنعين عن عذابه عز وجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r1.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r1.claim: Traditionists portray Qarūn as Israel’s most learned man after Moses and Aaron, learned in Torah, handsome, wealthy, pleasant-voiced, and transgressive.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r1.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r2.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r2.claim: The account says God commanded blue threads at the four corners of Israelite garments to remind them of Him and revelation descending from heaven; Moses proposed green garments, but God warned that disobedience in a small command foretold disobedience in a great one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r2.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r3.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r3.claim: Qarūn refused the garment command, saying only gods use such tokens to distinguish themselves; the account calls this the beginning of his rebellion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r3.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r4.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r4.claim: After the sea crossing, Aaron received the high priesthood; Qarūn resented Moses’ message and Aaron’s priesthood and demanded proof that God had appointed Aaron.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r4.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r5.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r5.claim: Moses set the leaders’ staffs in his worship tent overnight; Aaron’s almond staff sprouted leaves, but Qarūn dismissed the sign as magic.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r5.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r6.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r6.claim: Qarūn separated from Moses with his followers and continually harassed him; Moses bore it because of kinship, while Qarūn grew more defiant and hostile.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r6.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r7.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r7.claim: Qarūn built a house with a gold door and gold-plated walls, where Israel’s leaders came morning and evening for food and conversation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p223#2/r7.anchor: قال أهل العلم بالأخبار: كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى وهارون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r1.speaker: وفي رواية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r1.claim: One version says the earth swallowed Qarūn’s bed first and then took him and his companions progressively to the knees, waist, and neck as they begged Moses; Qarūn appealed to God and kinship seventy times, but Moses ignored him in anger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r1.anchor: وفي رواية: كان على سريره وفرشه فأخذته حتى غيبت سريره ثم قال: يا أرض خذيهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r2.speaker: الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r2.claim: God reproached Moses for his hard heart, saying Qarūn had appealed seventy times without relief, and that He would have answered if Qarūn had appealed to Him once.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r2.anchor: وأوحى الله إلى موسى ما أغلظ قلبك استغاث بك سبعين مرة فلم تغثه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r3.speaker: بعض الآثار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r3.claim: Some traditions add God’s declaration that He would not make the earth obedient to anyone after Moses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r3.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار: لا أجعل الأرض بعدك طوعا لأحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r4.claim: Qatāda says Qarūn sinks a man’s height into the earth each day and will not reach its bottom before the Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: خسف به فهو يتجلجل في الأرض كل يوم قامة رجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r5.claim: When Israelites whispered that Moses had invoked the sinking only to seize Qarūn’s estate, Moses prayed and God sank his house, treasures, and wealth as well.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r5.anchor: وأصبحت بنو إسرائيل يتناجون فيما بينهم أن موسى إنما دعا على قارون ليستبد بداره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r6.claim: Fiʾa means a group, and those who could not help Qarūn could not protect him from God’s sinking.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r6.anchor: {فما كان له من فئة} جماعة، {ينصرونه من دون الله} يمنعونه من الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r7.claim: Al-muntaṣirīn means those able to defend themselves against the sinking that struck them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p224#2/r7.anchor: {وما كان من المنتصرين} الممتنعين مما نزل به من الخسف

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r1.claim: A report says Qarun harassed Moses, agreed to pay one in a thousand after the zakat command, then plotted to discredit him by bribing a woman to accuse him falsely; Moses summoned her and she exposed Qarun's bribe.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r1.anchor: روي أنه كان يؤذي موسى عليه السلام كل وقت وهو يداريه لقرابته حتى نزلت الزكاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r2.claim: In the report, Moses prayed after the false accusation was exposed; God commanded the earth to take Qarun, who sank in stages while pleading, and God rebuked Moses for not showing mercy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r2.anchor: فأوحى إليه أن مر الأرض بما شئت

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r3.claim: When the Israelites said Moses had done this to inherit Qarun's wealth, Moses prayed to God, who caused Qarun's house and possessions to sink as well.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r3.anchor: ثم قال بنو إسرائيل: إنما فعله ليرثه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r4.claim: A فئة is a group of helpers, from a verb meaning to incline or bend something.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r4.anchor: أعوان مشتقة من فأوت رأسه إذا ميلته

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r5.claim: No group could rescue Qarun by warding off God's punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r5.anchor: { ينصرونه من دون الله } فيدفعون عنه عذابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r6.claim: He could not defend himself: one who defeats an enemy is said to help and then prevail against him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:81/r6.anchor: الممتنعين منه من قولهم نصره من عدوه فانتصر إذا منعه منه فامتنع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r1.claim: God's punishment followed Qarun's reasoning that led him to disbelief and caused him and his great house to sink into the earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r1.anchor: فخسفنا } أي بما لنا من العظمة { به وبداره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r2.claim: The house was immense, matching his wealth and adornment and holding many people and possessions, so its destruction cannot be read as looting his property.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r2.anchor: لئلا يقول قائل : إن الخسف به كان للرغبة في أخذ أمواله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r3.speaker: أهل الأخبار
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r3.claim: Biqāʿī says historical reporters placed Qarun among Moses' people and very near him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r3.anchor: وهو من قوم موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام وقريب منه جدا على ما نقله أهل الأخبار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r4.claim: The episode warns Muhammad's community not to reject the mercy brought by his message: prophets do not instill guidance in enemies' hearts or shield the condemned from ruin or intercede for them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r4.anchor: فإياكم يا أمة هذا النبي أن تردوا ما آتاكم من الرحمة برسالته فتهلكوا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r5.claim: The added من strengthens the denial that any human faction would come to Qarun's rescue, despite the assumption that notables have supporters.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r5.anchor: وأكد النفي لما استقر في الأذهان أن الأكابر منصورون بزيادة الجار في قوله : { من فئة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r6.claim: فئة means a group of people; its original image is a flock of birds, named for repeatedly and quickly returning to the place it left.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r6.anchor: وأصل الفئة الجماعة من الطير كأنها سميت بذلك لكثرة رجوعها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r7.claim: Those who shared Qarun's outlook perished, while God's allies feared Him and would not petition for Qarun; Qarun had lost sight of the truth as in the preceding verse.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r7.anchor: لأن من كان على مثل رأيه هلك , ومن كان من أولياء الله راقب الله في أمره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r8.claim: Qarun could not defend himself by his own strength.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p521/r8.anchor: أي هو { من المنتصرين * } لأنفسهم بقوتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r1.speaker: أهل العلم بالأخبار
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r1.claim: Al-Baghawī transmits from historians that Qarun was Israel's most learned man after Moses, a leading Torah reader, handsome and wealthy, before he became rebellious; his first defiance was the tassel command.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r1.anchor: قال البغوي : قال أهل العلم بالأخبار : كان قارون أعلم بني إسرائيل بعد موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام وأقرأهم للتوراة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r2.claim: In al-Baghawī's historical report, God ordered Moses to have four blue, sky-colored threads attached to garment corners as reminders that revelation came from heaven.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r2.anchor: أن يعلقوا في أرديتهم خيوطا أربعة , في كل طرف منها خيطا أخضر بلون السماء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r3.claim: Al-Baghawī's report says Moses proposed green garments because Israel belittled the small threads; God replied that disobedience in a small command predicts disobedience in a great one, and Qarun alone grew arrogant.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r3.anchor: يا موسى ! إن الصغير من أمري ليس بصغير , فإذا هم لم يطيعوني في الأمر الصغير لم يطيعوني في الأمر الكبير

BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r4.claim: After the sea crossing, Qarun complained that Aaron received the priesthood while he had no share despite reading the Torah; Moses said God, not he, had chosen Aaron.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r4.anchor: فلما قطع موسى ببني إسرائيل البحر جعل الحبورة , ولست في شيء وأنا أقرأ التوراة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r5.claim: In al-Baghawī's account, Qarun demanded proof, but Aaron's almond staff alone sprouted green leaves after the staffs were guarded overnight; Qarun dismissed it as no greater than Moses' magic.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r5.anchor: فأصبحت عصا هارون قد اهتز لها ورق أخضر , وكانت من اللوز , فقال قارون : والله ما هذا بأعجب مما تصنع من السحر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r6.claim: The report says Qarun boasted of various matters and made a grave accusation against Moses, after which God acted zealously for Moses and sank Qarun.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r6.anchor: وذكر أمورا مما كان يتعظم بها وأنه رمى موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام بعظيمة فحينئذ غار الله لموسى عليه الصلاة والسلام فخسف به

BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r7.claim: Biqāʿī says the fourth book of the Torah commands silk tassels as reminders to obey God's commands, avoid being led by the heart or one's own opinions, and be consecrated to God who brought Israel out of Egypt.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r7.anchor: والذي رأيته أنا في التوراة في السفر الرابع ما نصه : وكلم الرب موسى وقال له : كلم بني إسرائيل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r8.claim: The Torah passage identifies Korah as Qarun in Hebrew, son of Izhar, Kohath, and Levi, and names Dathan, Abiram, and On as rebels with him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r8.anchor: ومن بعد هذه الأمور شق قورح وهو اسم قارون بالعبرانية بن يصهر بن قاهث بن لاوى , ودائن وأبيروم ابنا أليب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r9.claim: Two hundred and fifty Israelites challenged Moses and Aaron, saying the whole congregation was holy and objecting that Aaron was elevated to priestly authority over offerings and the sanctuary.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p523/r9.anchor: وقاموا بين يدي موسى , وقم من بني إسرائيل عددهم مائتان وخمسون رجلا اجتمعوا إلى موسى وهارون وقالوا لهما : ليس حسبكما أن الجماعة كلها طاهرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r1.claim: In the Torah account, Moses says God will reveal the rightful priesthood in the morning; he reminds the Levites that God already set them apart and asks why they seek the priesthood too.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r1.anchor: سيظهر الرب ويبين لمن الكهنوت والرئاسة بكرة , ومن كان طاهرا فليتقرب إليه . ومن يختار الرب يتقرب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r2.claim: Dathan and Abiram refuse Moses' summons, accuse him of taking them from a land of milk and honey to die in the wilderness, and say he has not delivered the promised land, farms, or vineyards.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r2.anchor: وأرسل موسى ليدعو دائن وابيرم ابني أليب فقالا : لا تصعد إليك , أما تكتفيان بما صنعتما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r3.claim: Moses is deeply distressed and asks God not to accept the rebels' offerings, since he has wronged and harmed no one.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r3.anchor: فشق ذلك على موسى جدا , وقال أمام الرب : لا تقبل قرابينهم يا رب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r4.claim: Korah and his company, Aaron, and Moses assemble with censers; God's glory appears and He orders Moses and Aaron to withdraw because He will destroy the congregation, but they prostrate and plead that one man's sin not condemn all.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r4.anchor: وظهر مجد الرب للجماعة كلها , وكلم الرب موسى وهارون وقال لهما : تنحيا عن هذه الجماعة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r5.claim: God orders Israel to move away from Korah, Dathan, and Abiram's tents and touch none of their property; Moses says the earth opening will prove he was sent by God, not acting on his own.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r5.anchor: كلم الجماعة كلها وقل لهم : تنحوا عن خيم دائن وأبيروم وقورح , تنحوا عن خيم هؤلاء الفجار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r6.claim: Moses predicts that ordinary death would disprove his mission, while the earth swallowing the rebels, households, and livestock alive into Sheol would verify it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r6.anchor: إن مات هؤلاء مثل موت كل إنسان أو نزل بهم الموت مثل ما ينزل بجميع الناس فلم يرسلني الرب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r7.claim: The rebels and their possessions descend alive as the earth closes; Israelites flee in fear, fire consumes the 250 incense-bearers, and the people later accuse Moses and Aaron of killing God's congregation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p524/r7.anchor: وهرب جميع بني إسرائيل حيث سمعوا أصواتهم ورأوا ما قد صنع بهمن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r1.claim: The Torah narrative says God again orders Moses and Aaron away from the congregation; Moses sends Aaron with fire and incense to atone as sudden death spreads, and Aaron stands between dead and living until the plague stops.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r1.anchor: وقال موسى لهارون : خذ مجمرة بيك واجعل فيها نارا وبخورا , وانطلق مسرعا إلى الجماعة واستغفر لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r2.claim: Fourteen thousand seven hundred people die suddenly, apart from those swallowed by the earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r2.anchor: وكان عدد الذين ماتوا فجأة أربعة عشر ألفا وسبعمائة رجل غير المخسوف بهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r3.claim: God orders a staff from every tribe, with each man's name and Aaron's name on Levi's staff, to be placed before the testimony; the chosen man's staff will blossom and answer Israel's grumbling.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r3.anchor: خذ منهم عصا عصا من كل سبط , واكتب اسم كل رجل على عصاه , واكتب اسم هارون على عصا سبط لاوي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r4.claim: Moses finds that Aaron's staff has budded, grown branches and leaves, and borne almonds; God orders it kept as a sign for rebels and forbids non-Levites from tabernacle service.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r4.anchor: فرأى عصا هارون قد نضرت وأخرجت أغصانا وأورقت وأثمرت لوزا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r5.claim: The account then mentions Aaron's death on Mount Hor and his son Eleazar succeeding him in priestly office.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r5.anchor: ثم ذكر وزفاة هارون عليه السلام في هور الجبل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r6.claim: Biqāʿī compares Qarun's sinking with the Prophet's sign at Hunayn: the trunk yearned for him, and the Prophet offered to restore it or place it in Paradise, which it chose.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r6.anchor: وهو نحو مما فعل الله لنبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في حنين الجذع , وتخيير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم له

BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r7.claim: When Surāqa pursued Muhammad on the Hijra route, his horse's legs sank to its belly three times; the Prophet of mercy spared him, and Surāqa later accepted Islam and received the prophecy of Kisra's bracelets.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r7.anchor: حيث لحقه صلى الله عليه وسلم في طريق الهجرة ليرده فخسف بقوائم حصانه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r8.claim: Anas reports that a man of Banū al-Najjār who had read al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān and written for the Messenger fled to the People of the Book; after they honored him, God broke his neck and the earth twice expelled his buried body. Biqāʿī says Muslim reported it in the two Ṣaḥīḥs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r8.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال : كان منا رجل من بني النجار قد قرأ البقرة وآل عمران

BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r9.speaker: أنس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r9.claim: A second report from Anas says a Christian man's body was expelled by the earth three times before people left it unburied; Biqāʿī attributes this report to al-Bukhārī's Ṣaḥīḥ.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p525/r9.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه مثله أيضا في رجل نصراني لفظته الأرض ثلاث مرات ثم تركوه

DURR-FULL:v6p442/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r1.claim: In the transmitted account, Moses asks God to empower him over Qarun; God tells him to command the earth, which obeys as Moses orders it to swallow Qarun, his house, and his companions. God says He would have shown mercy had Qarun called on Him.
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r1.anchor: فأوحى الله إليه: أن مر الأرض بما شئت تطعك فجاء موسى إلى قارون فلما رآه قارون عرف الغضب في وجهه

DURR-FULL:v6p442/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r2.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r2.claim: Abu Imran al-Jawni adds that Moses was told no one would worship the earth after him.
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عمران الجوني: فقيل لموسى: لا أعبد الأرض بعدك

DURR-FULL:v6p442/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun was swallowed down to the lowest earth.
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض} قال: خسف به إلى الأرض السفلى

DURR-FULL:v6p442/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r4.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r4.claim: Samura b. Jundub reports that Qarun and his people sink a man's height each day and will not reach the lowest earth until the Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r4.anchor: عن سمرة بن جندب قال: يخسف بقارون وقومه في كل يوم قدر قامة

DURR-FULL:v6p442/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r5.claim: Qatada says Qarun sinks by a man's height every day, continuing to sink without reaching the bottom until the Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r5.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه قال: ذكر لنا أنه يخسف به كل يوم قامة وأنه يتجلجل فيها

DURR-FULL:v6p442/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives the same report: Qarun sinks a man's height each day and does not reach the bottom until the Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه مثله

DURR-FULL:v6p442/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r7.claim: Qatada says God commanded the earth to obey Moses for an hour.
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه قال: إن الله أمر الأرض أن تطيعه ساعة

DURR-FULL:v6p442/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r8.speaker: مالك بن دينار
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r8.claim: Malik b. Dinar says Qarun sinks a man's height each day.
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r8.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار رضي الله عنه: أن قارون يخسف به كل يوم قامة

DURR-FULL:v6p442/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r9.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r9.claim: Ikrima reports that Qarun begged Moses for mercy as he sank; Moses did not answer, and God said Qarun would have received mercy if he had called on God.
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r9.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: لما خسف بقارون فهو يذهب وموسى قريب منه قال: يا موسى ادع ربك يرحمني

DURR-FULL:v6p442/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r10.speaker: عون بن عبد الله القاري
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r10.claim: A report reaching Awn b. Abd Allah says Moses commanded the earth twice to swallow Qarun up to his knees and then completely; God said His heart was hard, since He would have answered Qarun's plea, and Moses replied that he acted in anger for God.
DURR-FULL:v6p442/r10.anchor: عن عون بن عبد الله القاري عامل عمر بن عبد العزيز على ديوان فلسطين أنه بلغه: أن الله عز وجل أمر الأرض أن تطيع موسى

DURR-FULL:v6p443/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p443/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p443/r1.claim: Qatada says Qarun had no force or protection with which to defend himself from God.
DURR-FULL:v6p443/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان من المنتصرين} قال: ما كانت عنده منعة يمتنع بها من الله تعالى

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the earth swallowed Qarun by stages, first to the heels, then the knees and neck, before swallowing him completely.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : فخسفنا به وبداره الارض قال : قيل للارض : خذيهم فاخذتهم الى اعقابهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports that God gave Moses command over the earth, which swallowed Qarun despite his pleas. Later, God rebuked Moses when Israelites suffering hunger had appealed to Moses rather than God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : اوحى الله الى موسى ما يبكيك ؟ قد امرت الارض ان تطيعك فامرها بما شئت

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r3.speaker: يزيد الرقاشي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r3.claim: Yazid al-Raqashi reports that Moses struck Qarun's face with his sandals as the earth swallowed him to the neck; God then reproached Moses for refusing his plea for mercy.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r3.anchor: عن يزيد الرقاشي ان موسى لما دعا على قارون فابتلعته الارض الى عنقه اخذ نعليه فخفق بهما وجهه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r4.claim: Al-Suddi reports that Qarun bribed Shirta with two thousand dirhams to accuse Moses of seduction; she repented, confessed the scheme publicly, and Moses prayed against Qarun.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r4.anchor: عن السدي فخسفنا به وبداره الارض قال : فبغى على موسى فانطلق الى زانية يقال لها : شيرتا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r5.speaker: موسى
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r5.claim: In al-Suddi's account, Moses says the prescribed penalty for a married adulterer is stoning, and confirms it applies even if the offender is himself.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3016/r5.anchor: فقال قارون : يا موسى ، ما انزل الله في الزاني : قال : الرجم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3017/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3017/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3017/r1.claim: The woman admits Qarun paid her to accuse Moses; Moses commands the earth to swallow Qarun and his house despite his pleas, and God says He would have answered Qarun had Qarun called on Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3017/r1.anchor: قال عومي يا شيرتا فاخبري بني اسرائيل بما اراد منك موسى ، فقالت : ان قارون اعطاني الفي درهم ان اتي الملا من بني اسرائيل اذا جلس موسى

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3017/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3017/r2.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3017/r2.claim: Ata reports that Qarun paraded in purple with four thousand attendants to draw attention from Moses' teaching, then challenged Moses to a prayer contest; Moses' prayer caused the earth to swallow Qarun, his followers, and their wealth in stages.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3017/r2.anchor: حدثني عطاء كان خلقا من موسى ان يخرج بني اسرائيل في يوم يعظهم فيه فاذا علم بذلك قارون ، خرج في اربعة الاف

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qarun was Moses' cousin, had pursued and amassed knowledge, then became arrogant and jealous and resisted Moses' proposed alms levy.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قال : ان قارون كان من قوم موسى وكان ابن عمه وكان تتبع العلم حتى جمع علما

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r2.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account, Moses says the law requires stoning a married adulterer and cutting off a thief's hand, even if Moses himself committed the offense.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r2.anchor: وامرني في الزاني اذا زنى وقد احصن ان يرجم فقالوا : وان كنت انت ؟ قال : نعم . وفي السارق اذا سرق ان يقطع

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Qarun recruited a woman to falsely accuse Moses, but she confessed that she had been paid and affirmed Moses was God's messenger; God then empowered Moses to command the earth to swallow Qarun.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r3.anchor: فجاءت فقالوا ما تشهدين على موسى ؟ فقال لها موسى : انشدك بالله الا ما صدقت فقالت : اما اذا انشدتني بالله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r4.claim: After Qarun's destruction, Israelites suffered severe hunger; Ibn Abbas's report says God told Moses that had the people called on God, He would have answered them.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3018/r4.anchor: فاصاب بني اسرائيل بلاء وجوع شديد فاتوا موسى فقالوا : ادع لنا ، فدعى الله ، فقال الله : اتدعوني لقوم قد اظلم ما بيني وبينهم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل الهاشمي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019/r1.claim: Abdullah ibn al-Harith reports that Qarun's house had a gold door and gold-plated walls, and Israelite leaders regularly ate and talked at his home; Qarun then tried to frame Moses through a woman, who repented and cleared him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019/r1.anchor: قال : بلغنا انه اوتي الكنوز والمال حتى جعل باب داره من ذهب وجعل داره كلها من صفائح الذهب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل الهاشمي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019/r2.claim: Abdullah ibn al-Harith reports that Moses prayed for power over Qarun, then ordered the earth to swallow him and his companions as Qarun pleaded for mercy.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019/r2.anchor: فاوحى الله اليه ان مر الارض بما شئت تطيعك ، قال : فجاء موسى الى قارون ، فلما راه قارون عرف الغضب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r1.claim: Abu Imran al-Jawni reports that Moses was told the earth would never again be made to swallow anyone after him.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r1.anchor: وقال ابو عمران الجوني : فقيل لموسى : لا اعيد الارض بعدك لاحد ابدا .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the earth into which Qarun sank as the seventh, lowest earth.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : فخسفنا به وبداره الارض قال : ارض السفلى السابعة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r3.claim: Qatada says Qarun is swallowed by a measure of one stature every day and keeps sinking without reaching the bottom until the Resurrection.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قوله تعالى : فخسفنا به وبداره الارض قال : ذكر لنا انه يخسف به كل يوم قامة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r4.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r4.claim: Samura ibn Jundab reports, through Qatada, that Qarun and his people sink by a stature each day and will not reach the lowest earth until the Resurrection.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r4.anchor: ثنا قتادة ، عن ابي ميمونة ، عن سمرة بن جندب ، انه قال : يخسف بقارون وقومه في كل يوم قدر قامة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r5.claim: Qatada reports that God ordered the earth to obey Moses for an hour.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r5.anchor: ثنا قتادة ، قال : ان الله امر الارض ان تطيعه ساعة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عوف القاري
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r6.claim: Ibn Awf al-Qari reports that Moses commanded the earth to swallow Qarun by stages; God said that He would have answered Qarun had Qarun appealed to Him, and Moses said he acted in anger for God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3019#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن شهاب اخبرني عبد الله بن عوف القاري عامل عمر بن عبد العزيز على ديوان فلسطين انه بلغه ان الله تبارك وتعالى

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3020/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3020/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3020/r1.claim: Qatada explains فئة as an army that could help Qarun apart from God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3020/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله اي جند ينصرونه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3020/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3020/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3020/r2.claim: Qatada says Qarun had no means of protection by which to defend himself against God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3020/r2.anchor: وما كان من المنتصرين قال : ما كانت ، عنده منعة يمتنع بها من الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r7.claim: The ف marks the punishment’s immediate sequence after Qarun’s proud display, the crowd’s wish to resemble him, and the scholars’ correction, while those wishful onlookers saw his punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r7.anchor: دلت الفاء على تعقيب ساعة خروج قارون في ازدهائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r8.claim: Khasf is the turning of the earth’s surface into its interior, or the reverse; the subsidence occurs through earthquake force, while eclipsing the sun is a figurative use.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r8.anchor: والخسف : انقلاب بعض ظاهر الأرض إلى باطنها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r9.claim: The bāʾ means accompaniment: God made the earth sink together with Qarun and his house.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r9.anchor: والباء في قوله { فخسفنا به } باء المصاحبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r10.claim: This extraordinary subsidence affected Qarun and those immediately with him, not the wider area, and was a miracle for Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r10.anchor: وهذا الخسف خارق للعادة لأنه لم يتناول غير قارون ومن ظاهره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r11.speaker: سفر العدد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r11.claim: Numbers 16 recounts Korah’s opposition to Moses, Moses’ warning and call for people to leave their tents, the earth swallowing Korah’s group and property alive, and fire destroying 250 men.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r11.anchor: جاء في الإصحاح السادس عشر من سفر العدد أن قورح ( وهو قارون ) ومن معه لما آذوا موسى كما تقدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r12.claim: Qarun relied on many chiefs among the Levites and others who backed his challenge to Moses; the earth swallowed them with him, so none could help him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r12.anchor: وقد كان قارون معتزا على موسى بالطائفة التي كانت شايعته على موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r13.claim: The faction he had prepared to support him against Moses perished with him, so he had no helper apart from God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r13.anchor: فلذلك قال الله تعالى { فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r14.claim: انتصر means to obtain victory: Qarun’s allies did not rescue him, and he could not save himself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p184/r14.anchor: يقال : انتصر فلان ، إذا حصل له النصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r6.claim: A report says Qarun wronged Moses and accused him through a woman; Moses sought God's aid, and the earth swallowed Qarun and his followers gradually as they pleaded.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r6.anchor: أن موسى عليه السلام لما أمضه فعل قارون به وتعديه عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r7.claim: In the same report, God says He would have shown mercy and relieved them had they appealed to Him or repented.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r7.anchor: لو بي استغاثوا أو إلي تابوا لرحمتهم وكشفت ما بهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r8.speaker: قتادة ومالك بن دينار
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r8.claim: Qatada and Malik ibn Dinar transmit that Qarun sinks one stature each day until the Resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة ومالك بن دينار: روي لنا أنه يخسف به كل يوم قامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r9.claim: A “fiah” is a supporting group to which someone seeking help turns.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r9.anchor: الجماعة الناصرة التي يفيء إليها الإنسان الطالب للنصرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r10.claim: The episode follows the sea crossing: transmitters said Qarun had preserved and recited the Torah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p301/r10.anchor: وقصة قارون هي بعد جوازهم اليم لأن الرواة ذكروا أنه كان ممن حفظ التوراة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r1.claim: After Qarun's earlier plot against Moses, God said the earth would obey Moses. Moses told it to seize Qarun; it swallowed his throne and then him as he pleaded. God reproached Moses, saying He would have answered Qarun had he called on Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r1.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إليه إني قد أمرت الأرض أن تطيعك فمرها فقال موسى يا أرض خذيه فأخذته حتى غيبت سريره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the earth swallowed Qarun down to the lowest earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس فخسفت به الأرض إلى الأرض السفلى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r3.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r3.claim: Samura ibn Jundab says Qarun sinks a man's height each day until he reaches the lowest earth on Judgment Day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r3.anchor: وقال سمرة بن جندب إنه يخسف به كل يوم قامة فتبلغ به الأرض السفلى يوم القيامة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r4.claim: Muqatil says God sank Qarun's house and wealth three days after Israelites accused Moses of doing so to take them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p244#2/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل فلما هلك قارون قال بنو إسرائيل إنما أهلكه موسى ليأخذ ماله وداره فخسف الله بداره وماله بعده بثلاثة ايام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r1.claim: No group could protect Qarun from God.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r2.claim: He could not protect himself from the punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r2.anchor: أي من الممتنعين مما نزل به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r3.claim: Those who wished for Qarun's former position regretted it in the following verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p245/r3.anchor: ثم أعلمنا أن المتمنين مكانه ندموا على ذلك التمني بالآية التي تلي هذه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r1.claim: In a report in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet says a man dragging his garment was swallowed by the earth and will keep sinking until resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r1.anchor: عن سالم -أن أباه حدثه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r2.claim: Al-Bukhari also transmits a similar version from Abu Hurayra about a man swallowed by the earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r2.anchor: عن سالم عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، نحوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي سعيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r3.claim: Ahmad reports that a man in two green cloaks swaggered, so God ordered the earth to seize him; he sinks until resurrection. Ibn Kathir grades the chain hasan and says Ahmad alone transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال: قال رسول الله (4) صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r4.claim: Abu Ya'la reports Anas's account of a man who swaggered in two cloaks and was swallowed, sinking until resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r4.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r5.speaker: نوفل بن مساحق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r5.claim: A strange report says a handsome, tall young man in Najran claimed God marveled at him, then shrank to a handspan and was carried away by a relative.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r5.anchor: عن نوفل بن مساحق قال: رأيت شابا في مسجد نجران، فجعلت أنظر إليه وأتعجب من طوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r6.claim: They say Qarun bribed a prostitute to falsely accuse Moses; she confessed, Moses prayed against Qarun, and God ordered the earth to obey him and swallow Qarun and his house.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p256/r6.anchor: فعن ابن عباس والسدي: أن قارون أعطى امرأة بغيا مالا على أن تبهت موسى بحضرة الملأ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p257/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p257/r1.speaker: قول غير مسمى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p257/r1.claim: An alternative account says Qarun paraded in purple-dyed garments on gray mules with servants; Moses reproached him, Qarun challenged him to mutual prayers, and Moses called the earth to swallow him, his people, and his treasures in stages.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p257/r1.anchor: وقيل: إن قارون لما خرج على قومه في زينته تلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p257/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p257/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
